name: Stale mega-PR reconcile: measure the conflict surface, then apply a per-file-class recipe
description: Blueprint 37 of 96 (BP-PLN-05). Rescues ONE unmergeable stale branch. The distinctive mechanism is that the conflict surface is MEASURED on a throwaway merge before any resolution is planned - a +72k-line / 288-commit PR had a five-file surface - and every conflicted file is then resolved by its CLASS (deps / machinery / tests / source) rather than by judgement. Line count is banned as an estimator and a guessed runtime-dependent expected value is treated as fabrication, so it is deferred to the owner instead.

branch.description: The stale branch or PR head to reconcile

base.description: The base ref the branch must land on

intent_statement.description: What the branch was FOR. If the intent is itself obsolete the branch is closed, not reconciled (contraindication).

conflict_file_budget.description: Above this measured surface the reconcile is escalated rather than attempted

file_classes.description: The four resolution classes; each conflicted file is assigned exactly one

surveyor.description: Runs the mechanical measurement only - throwaway merge, unmerged-path count, A/M/D composition. Emits numbers, never resolutions.

resolver.description: Resolves ONE conflicted file by its declared class recipe; may not widen scope to a file it was not assigned.

owner.description: The human owner - the only role that may pin a runtime-dependent expected value or close the branch

surface-measured.expression: surface_from_throwaway_merge == true AND estimated_from_line_count == false AND merge_aborted == true

stages.title: Throwaway merge: count the UNMERGED paths, then abort

work_unit.title: Measure the real conflict surface of a stale branch on a throwaway merge
work_unit.question_or_target: On a throwaway branch cut from base, run a no-commit no-ff merge of the stale branch, count `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`, record the A/M/D composition from the merge-base diff, then abort the merge. Report the UNMERGED-path count and never the +/- line count as the estimate of work.
work_unit.evidence_requirement: the literal `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` output and the `git diff --name-status <merge-base> <head>` A/M/D tally, both re-runnable, plus proof the merge was aborted (a clean `git status` on the throwaway branch)
tests_required: both-states control: a branch with a KNOWN conflicted file must report count >= 1, and a fast-forwardable branch must report 0 - a measurement that returns 0 in both states measures nothing
the reported count must differ from the changed-line count on a branch whose additions dominate (added files never conflict)
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reviewer who re-runs the merge measurement on the same two refs and compares the unmerged-path set, not the summary
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:AUD-0002 emitted only when conflict-surface.json exists, parses against output_schema, carries the raw unmerged-path list, and the throwaway branch is clean; otherwise FAILED:AUD-0002 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot; a second failure to construct the throwaway merge means the refs are wrong - re-fetch and re-derive rather than retrying the same command

stages.title: Optional S0b: if `git log B..A` is empty then B contains A - close A instead
The surface must come from the merge, not from the diff size
A surface above the budget is escalated, not attempted
One resolver per conflicted file, dispatched by file CLASS

body.title: Apply the class recipe: deps->take base wholesale; machinery->keep base unless the branch's intent is to change it; tests->graft only self-contained ones; source->manual

stages.title: Guessing a runtime-dependent expected value is fabrication; deleting deferred machinery is scope theft
Hand the runtime-dependent assertions and the ungraftable tests back to the owner, in writing
stages.prompt: These conflicted items cannot be resolved without guessing: runtime-dependent expected values, and tests that depend on the other side's helpers and would not compile if grafted. Pin the values, or accept them as PR-disclosed follow-ups.

impact.blast_radius: a throwaway measurement branch plus writes under command-center/reconcile/**; the stale branch itself is never force-pushed by this workflow

worked_example.scenario: A branch 288 commits behind base whose PR shows +72,431 / -1,208 across 1,188 files.
worked_example.step_1_measure: throwaway merge -> `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` returns 5 paths: package.json, package-lock.json, .github/workflows/quality.yml, src/nav/items.ts, src/nav/items.test.ts
worked_example.step_2_compose: merge-base diff A=1,141 M=42 D=5 - the additions are what made the PR look unlandable and they cannot conflict
worked_example.step_3_classify: deps -> package.json + lockfile (branch has NO unique deps, so base is the superset: take base wholesale); machinery -> quality.yml (keep base, the branch's intent does not touch CI); source -> src/nav/items.ts (manual); tests -> src/nav/items.test.ts
worked_example.step_4_defer: items.test.ts asserts `expect(navItems.length).toBe(10)` while base's new code makes it 11. The workflow does NOT guess 11 - fabrication-gate blocks and defer-runtime-values hands it to the owner or to CI.
worked_example.measured_outcome: reconcile cost = 5 files, not 1,188; the line count over-estimated the surface by ~237x on the file axis

contraindications: NOT for a fresh PR - there is no stale surface to measure
NOT when the branch's intent is itself obsolete - close it instead of reconciling (stopping rule intent-obsolete)
NOT a substitute for CI on semantic conflict - this blueprint only addresses textual conflict
x_extensions.distinctive_mechanism: surface measured on a throwaway merge BEFORE planning; resolution dispatched by file class; runtime-dependent values deferred rather than guessed
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-PLN-03 orders N already-mergeable PRs; this rescues ONE unmergeable stale branch and its defining act is a measurement that replaces an estimate.
